할아버지.note: grandfather; also used for any elderly man

할머니.note: grandmother; also used for any elderly woman

라면.l: ramen (Japanese ラーメン, from Chinese 拉麵)

과일.note: naturalised in Korean; related to the Sino-Korean 果實 (과실), but no longer read that way

점퍼.l: jacket (Korean 점퍼, not a British jumper)

구두.l: kutsu (Japanese くつ) — the usual attribution, though not settled

길을 찾다.note: literally "to look for the road" — to find one's way

길을 잃다.note: literally "to lose the road" — to get lost

마르다.note: native verb 마르다 (to dry, to thin)

먼지를 털다.note: literally "to beat the dust out" — to dust something down

발이 넓다.note: literally "the feet are wide" — to know a great many people

귀가 얇다.note: literally "the ears are thin" — easily persuaded

눈이 높다.note: literally "the eyes are high" — to have exacting standards

손이 크다.note: literally "the hand is big" — generous, cooks and gives in quantity

입이 가볍다.note: literally "the mouth is light" — cannot keep a secret

콧대가 높다.note: literally "the bridge of the nose is high" — haughty

배가 아프다.note: literally "the belly hurts" — to be envious of someone else's good fortune

발 벗고 나서다.note: literally "to step out with bare feet" — to throw oneself into helping

어깨가 무겁다.note: literally "the shoulders are heavy" — to carry a weighty responsibility

낯이 익다.note: literally "the face is ripe" — to look familiar

낯이 설다.note: literally "the face is unripe" — to look unfamiliar

눈코 뜰 새 없이 바쁘다.note: literally "no time to open eyes or nose" — frantically busy

귀를 기울이다.note: literally "to tilt the ear" — to listen closely

입을 모으다.note: literally "to gather mouths" — to say the same thing in unison

손을 씻다.note: literally "to wash one's hands" — to break with a bad business for good

발을 끊다.note: literally "to cut one's feet" — to stop going somewhere entirely

가슴이 치밀다.note: literally "the chest surges" — emotion welling up

눈길을 끌다.note: literally "to pull the gaze" — to catch the eye

그림의 떡.note: literally "rice cake in a painting" — desirable and out of reach

누워서 떡 먹기.note: literally "eating rice cake lying down" — even easier than that

우물 안 개구리.note: literally "a frog in a well" — someone who mistakes their corner for the world

티끌 모아 태산.note: literally "specks gathered make a great mountain" — many small amounts add up

뼈가 있다.note: literally "there is a bone in it" — a remark with a hidden barb

가슴을 치다.note: literally "to strike the chest" — to beat one's breast in grief

손을 잡다.note: literally "to take hands" — to join forces

뜸을 들이다.note: literally "to let the rice steam" — to hold off and keep people waiting

허리띠를 졸라매다.note: literally "to tighten the belt" — to cut back and endure

그러므로.note: native connective — 그러하다 + -므로 (because it is so)

왜냐하면.note: native connective — 왜 (why) + -냐 하면 (if one asks)

그럼에도 불구하고.note: native + Sino — 그럼에도 (even so) + 不拘하고 (without regard)

말하자면.note: native — 말하다 + -자면 (if one is to say)

통틀어.note: native — 통 (whole) + 틀다 (to turn), taken all together
